- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to cap the peak; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% and smooth the slope downward.
- If sentiment is positive (avg > 0.1) and model forecast is below recent 10-day average, model underestimates upward momentum; raise forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven rally.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lead time to forecast horizon to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by 2–4% over 30-day horizon, apply a 1–2% upward bias to all 30-day points, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, don’t extrapolate; instead, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak to avoid over-optimism.
